subproblems.title: Finite monomial expansion of a homogeneous binary form
subproblems.statement: Let n be a natural number and Q an element of HeckeEis.BinaryForm ℂ n. For r ∈ Fin(n+1), define d_r : Fin 2 →₀ ℕ by d_r = Finsupp.single 0 r.val + Finsupp.single 1 (n−r.val). Then, in MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℂ, Q.val = Σ_{r∈Fin(n+1)} coeff d_r(Q.val) • monomial d_r 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (Q : ↥(HeckeEis.BinaryForm ℂ n)), Q.val = ∑ r : Fin (n + 1), MvPolynomial.coeff (Finsupp.single (0 : Fin 2) r.val + Finsupp.single (1 : Fin 2) (n - r.val)) Q.val • MvPolynomial.monomial (Finsupp.single (0 : Fin 2) r.val + Finsupp.single (1 : Fin 2) (n - r.val)) (1 : ℂ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
1. Fix n and Q. For r ∈ Fin(n+1), put d_r = single 0 r.val + single 1 (n−r.val), and put m_r = monomial d_r 1. Since r.val < n+1, we have r.val ≤ n. Evaluating the single functions gives d_r(0)=r.val and d_r(1)=n−r.val. The degree of a finitely supported exponent on Fin 2 is the sum of its values at 0 and 1, so degree(d_r)=r.val+(n−r.val)=n.
2. Let S = Σ_r coeff d_r(Q.val) • m_r. Fix any exponent d : Fin 2 →₀ ℕ. Coefficients preserve finite sums and scalar multiplication, and the monomial coefficient formula gives coeff d(m_r)=1 if d_r=d and 0 otherwise. Consequently coeff d(S)=Σ_r coeff d_r(Q.val)·(if d_r=d then 1 else 0).
3. Suppose degree(d)≠n. Since Q belongs to the degree-n homogeneous submodule, coeff d(Q.val)=0. Step 1 shows d_r≠d for every r, so every summand in step 2 is zero. Thus coeff d(S)=0=coeff d(Q.val).
4. Suppose degree(d)=n. This means d(0)+d(1)=n. Hence d(0)≤n and n−d(0)=d(1). Let r₀ ∈ Fin(n+1) have value d(0); its required bound follows from d(0)≤n. The exponents d_{r₀} and d agree at 0 and at 1. These are all elements of Fin 2, so finitely supported function extensionality gives d_{r₀}=d.
5. If d_r=d, evaluation at 0 gives r.val=d(0)=r₀.val. Extensionality of Fin yields r=r₀. Therefore the finite sum in step 2 reduces to its term at r₀ and equals coeff d_{r₀}(Q.val)=coeff d(Q.val).
6. The two cases prove coeff d(Q.val)=coeff d(S) for every exponent d. Polynomial coefficient extensionality gives Q.val=S, which is the asserted equality.
proof_key_steps: Compute the coordinates and degree of every exponent d_r.
Compute coefficients of the proposed sum using coefficient linearity and the monomial formula.
Use homogeneity to handle exponents of degree different from n.
Represent each degree-n exponent uniquely as d_r.
Reduce the coefficient sum to one term and apply polynomial extensionality.

subproblems.title: Coefficients of a linear image are fixed finite linear combinations
subproblems.statement: Let n be a natural number, V = HeckeEis.BinaryForm ℂ n, A : V →ₗ[ℂ] V, and e : Fin 2 →₀ ℕ. For r ∈ Fin(n+1), put d_r = Finsupp.single 0 r.val + Finsupp.single 1 (n−r.val). There exists c : Fin(n+1) → ℂ, independent of Q, such that every Q ∈ V satisfies coeff e((A Q).val) = Σ_{r∈Fin(n+1)} c(r)·coeff d_r(Q.val).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (A : ↥(HeckeEis.BinaryForm ℂ n) →ₗ[ℂ] ↥(HeckeEis.BinaryForm ℂ n)) (e : Fin 2 →₀ ℕ), ∃ c : Fin (n + 1) → ℂ, ∀ Q : ↥(HeckeEis.BinaryForm ℂ n), MvPolynomial.coeff e (A Q).val = ∑ r : Fin (n + 1), c r * MvPolynomial.coeff (Finsupp.single (0 : Fin 2) r.val + Finsupp.single (1 : Fin 2) (n - r.val)) Q.val
subproblems.natural_proof:
1. Fix n, A, and e, and write V=HeckeEis.BinaryForm ℂ n. For each r ∈ Fin(n+1), define d_r=single 0 r.val+single 1 (n−r.val) and m_r=monomial d_r 1. We have r.val≤n, d_r(0)=r.val, and d_r(1)=n−r.val, so degree(d_r)=n. The monomial coefficient formula shows that every nonzero coefficient of m_r has exponent d_r and therefore degree n. Thus m_r is homogeneous of degree n. Let b_r ∈ V be m_r regarded as an element of this homogeneous submodule.
2. Define c(r)=coeff e((A b_r).val). This defines c : Fin(n+1) → ℂ using only n, A, and e, before any choice of Q.
3. Fix Q ∈ V and set a_r=coeff d_r(Q.val). Apply lct_monomial_expansion to obtain Q.val=Σ_r a_r • m_r. The inclusion of V into MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℂ preserves finite sums and scalar multiplication. Therefore this sum is the underlying polynomial of Σ_r a_r • b_r. Subtype extensionality now gives Q=Σ_r a_r • b_r in V.
4. Apply A to the equality in step 3. Since A is complex linear, it preserves the finite sum and each scalar multiple, giving A Q=Σ_r a_r • A b_r. Taking underlying polynomials and then coefficient e, using coefficient additivity and scalar compatibility, gives coeff e((A Q).val)=Σ_r a_r·coeff e((A b_r).val).
5. Substitute a_r=coeff d_r(Q.val) and the definition of c(r). Commutativity of complex multiplication changes each summand to c(r)·coeff d_r(Q.val). This proves the required identity for the arbitrary Q. Hence the function c defined in step 2 satisfies the universal identity and witnesses the existential conclusion.
proof_key_steps: Construct the degree-n monomials as elements b_r of the homogeneous submodule.
Define c(r) as the output coefficient of A(b_r), independently of Q.
Use the sibling expansion and subtype extensionality to expand Q inside V.
Apply linearity of A and of the coefficient functional.
Commute the complex factors and conclude the identity for every Q.
